newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha sags, distillate trade listless.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha sags, distillate trade listless.

text.p: Naphtha prices slid down in afternoon Tokyo trade while trade in middle distillates remained subdued on the back of ample domestic stocks, traders said on Thursday.
"I don't know anyone who has storage space available for spot imports of of kerosene or gas oil," one trader said. "Oil firms are having a hard time finding space for term lots."
Gas oil traders are focusing on opportunities to export to China rather than imports, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half August was indicated at $203.00/204.00 per tonne, down from Wednesday's $204.00/205.00.
Second-half August was quoted about 75 cents higher than the first half of the month. It was traded once at $205.75, and again at $206.00 in late Wednesday dealing.
"The tone of the market is a little weaker today," one naphtha trader said. "I wonder if naphtha prices will edge up towards the evening as it has done in the last couple of days."

An annual open-spec naphtha conference will be held in Tokyo on June 23 and 24, traders said. Participants are expected to discuss cargo specifications and quality inspection methods at the two-day meeting, they said.
